title: Complete (third-degree) heart block
summary: No impulse crosses the AV node. The atria beat on at the sinus rate while a slow escape rhythm drives the ventricles.
source: Slides 39-40 (third-degree AV block); 16, 20-21 (nodal and infranodal blocks)

events.label: Sinus beat
events.caption: The sinus node fires and the atria activate normally.

events.label: Block at the AV node
events.caption: The impulse reaches the AV node and goes no further. In complete heart block no atrial impulse crosses to the ventricles.
events.ecg: A P wave with no QRS after it.

events.label: Escape rhythm
events.caption: A pacemaker below the block takes over. This junctional escape focus fires at about 40 per minute and drives the ventricles through the normal conduction system.
events.ecg: A narrow QRS appears with no P wave before it: it is not related to the atria.

events.label: Atria carry on
events.caption: The sinus node keeps firing at its own rate, and each P wave is blocked at the AV node.
events.ecg: P waves march on at their own regular rate, unrelated to the QRS complexes: AV dissociation.

events.label: Next escape beat
events.caption: The escape rhythm fires again, slower than the atria. The atrial and ventricular rates are independent.
events.ecg: Atrial rate faster than ventricular rate, each running regularly on its own.

teaching_points: Third-degree AV block: no atrial impulse reaches the ventricles; atria and ventricles beat independently (AV dissociation) (slide 39).
The escape rhythm decides the QRS: a junctional focus above the bundle branches gives a narrow QRS, a ventricular focus gives a wide one, and the rate is slow (about 40 or less).
Nodal blocks are usually transient and have a more reliable junctional escape; infranodal blocks are less stable (slides 20-21).
